key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier neural operator reconstructs unsteady 3D floating-wind-turbine wakes from two observation planes and transfers learned dynamics from a 5 MW to a 22 MW turbine.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support downstream-inflow assessment in floating wind farms while reducing measurement and retraining needs.
method: Generate fixed and coupled surge–pitch wake data using large-eddy simulation with an actuator line model.
Combine 4D spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity and rotor-forced momentum-residual regularization.
Train on 5 MW cases, then use transfer learning to adapt to the 22 MW turbine.
evidence_signal: In simulation-based tests, 10% planar sampling nearly matched dense-sampling accuracy (relative L2 error 0.0689 vs 0.0684), and transfer learning reduced 22 MW streamwise-velocity error at St = 0.6 by 36% versus zero-shot inference.
watch_item: Fine-scale vortex breakdown remains damped, and validation beyond simulation-generated wakes is still needed.
paper_title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
